# dsh-openai-codex-image
A DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin that signs in with a **ChatGPT account** (Codex OAuth) and generates
images through the ChatGPT **subscription quota** instead of a paid API key.
English | 中文
## Why
OpenAI's `gpt-image-2` is documented for the paid API-key path (`api.openai.com`). If you already pa
y for ChatGPT, an agent that calls the image API pays for the same model twice. This plugin follows
the same route the Codex CLI uses:

…authenticated with the ChatGPT OAuth access token + `chatgpt_account_id`. Image calls ride the Chat
GPT subscription instead of API credits.
> This is an unofficial integration of a Codex CLI endpoint. It is not affiliated with OpenAI, and O
penAI may change the endpoint at any time. Make sure using it complies with the terms that apply to
nge the endpoint at any time. Make sure using it complies with the terms that apply to your account.
## Demo
Both images were generated with `generate_image` through a ChatGPT subscription account:
| `1024x1024` request (actual 1312x1199) | `1536x1024` + `quality=low` (actual 1672x941) |
## Features
- `generate_image` tool: prompt → PNG file in your workspace, displayed inline in chat when the acti

ve model accepts image input.
- `openai_account` tool: status / device-code login / poll / logout.
-
**Settings → ChatGPT Image** page: authorization status (source, account, plan, token expiry), the
device-code login flow, sign-out, and the current image defaults — the same-origin routes never retu

rn tokens.
- Auth resolution: plugin-owned OAuth record in DSH credentials first, then the local Cod

ex CLI login (`~/.codex/auth.json`, **read-only**).
- Automatic token refresh for the plugin-owned r

ecord (refreshed tokens are written back to the same DSH credential record).
- No hard dependency on
`@deepseek-ai/*` packages: the plugin only uses Node built-ins and the services on the DSH context,

so it works as a locally installed bundle.
- Original SVG icon, localized metadata (en / zh).
## Requirements
- DSH Desktop (or a DSH profile with the `credentials`, `attachments`, `workingDirectory` and `llm`

services).
- Node.js `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0`.
- A ChatGPT account that can use Codex, logged in eithe

r through:
- the Codex CLI (`codex login`), or
- this plugin's device-code flow.

### Account authorization
| Action | Purpose |

| `status` | Show auth source, account, plan, token expiry, image defaults |
| `login_start` | Start
OpenAI device-code login; returns `https://auth.openai.com/codex/device` plus an 8-character code |

| `login_poll` | Call after finishing browser login to exchange and store the token |
| `logout` |
Delete the plugin-owned credential (the Codex CLI login is left untouched) |
Device-code flow:

1. `openai_account(action="login_start")` → open the URL, enter the code;
2. complete the ChatGPT lo
uses that authorization.
### Settings page
DSH → Settings → **ChatGPT Image** shows the current authorization source, account, plan and token e
xpiry, starts the device-code login, confirms it, and signs the plugin-owned credential out. It read
s the plugin's own same-origin routes under `/api/openai-codex-image/*`; the page receives no tokens
(the account id is masked).
The page is the browser half of the bundle (`client.js`). Client bundles load when the host starts,
so **restart DSH Desktop after installing or upgrading this plugin** to see a new or changed setting
start DSH Desktop after installing or upgrading this plugin** to see a new or changed settings page.
## Authentication sources
1. **Plugin credential** — DSH credential record `openai-image/chatgpt` (`kind: "grant"`, payload `{
type: "oauth", access, refresh, expires, accountId, ... }`). Refreshed automatically 60 seconds bef

ore expiry; refreshed tokens replace the same record.
2. **Codex CLI** — `~/.codex/auth.json` (`auth
_mode: "chatgpt"`). Read-only: the plugin never writes to it, so token rotation in the Codex CLI sta
ys consistent. If it is expired, the plugin asks you to run `codex login` or use the device-code flo
consistent. If it is expired, the plugin asks you to run `codex login` or use the device-code flow.
## Security
- Tokens live only in the DSH credential store and in the Codex CLI's own `~/.codex/auth.json`; the

plugin never logs or copies them.
- `logout` removes only the plugin-owned record; run `codex logout

` separately to sign the Codex CLI out.
- Prompts are sent to OpenAI — that is inherent to image gen

eration.
- See SECURITY.md for reporting vulnerabilities.
